correctness.rationale: The original definition is sup_{0<=τ<=1} J^B_{X,t}(τ)^2/(1+τ²), with the monotone two-variable power mean M_t. For every t<=2, monotonicity and Qi–Yin–Liu Proposition 2 imply C_t^B(X)<=C_2(X)=C_NJ(X). Classical Clarkson bounds real ℓ_p(I), |I|>=2, and L_p[0,1] by 2^|2/p−1|. For 1<=p<=2, disjoint unit atoms or disjoint normalized half-interval indicators satisfy ||x+λy||_p>=1 for every real λ and have ||x±y||=2^(1/p). For 2<=p<∞, balanced unit two-coordinate/sign-half witnesses satisfy the Birkhoff smoothness criterion sum/integral |x|^(p−2)x y=0 and give ||x±y||=2^(1−1/p). For p=∞, the same sign-balanced pairs obey the direct max norm inequality >=1 and have both chords 2. Each equal-chord pair at τ=1 yields (||x±y||)^2/2, matching the upper value; p=2 and p=1 endpoints agree, and the −∞ power mean of equal positive numbers is that number. All quantifiers follow from actual finite-support/half-interval witnesses and global Clarkson inequality. No finite experiment is misused as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: The theorem does not assert t>2 for non-Hilbert 1<p<∞; endpoint lower witness alone does not provide corresponding upper bound there.
All spaces are real; complex Birkhoff variation and other measure geometries are outside the stated claim.
No formal proof assistant or independent peer verification has been performed; ordinary analytic identities were checked manually.
